Sibuna v0.3.2 completes console two-factor authentication. Account owners can replace
recovery codes or turn two-factor off, administrators can reset another account's factor, and
a lost or replaced console key no longer leaves accounts without a way back. Request
inspection, CRS behaviour and wire protocols are unchanged from v0.3.1.

Fixes:
- On a node whose console key is missing or different, a correct password for a two-factor
  account answered 503 without an audit record, while a wrong password answered 401. Both now
  receive the same audited refusal, and the node logs that it cannot read the factor.
- Accounts that had never enrolled saw "Two-factor configuration could not be loaded" and
  could not start enrollment from the console. Their status now reads as not enrolled.
- Authenticator entries are labelled with the username instead of a numeric account id.

Two-factor lifecycle:
- Account owners can replace every recovery code, or turn two-factor off, with their password
  and a current authenticator code or unused recovery code. Proofs are consumed under the same
  replay rules as sign-in. Turning two-factor off ends the account's sessions.
- A recovery code needs no console key, so after a key is lost or replaced an owner can sign
  in, turn two-factor off and enroll again under the new key.
- Administrators can reset another account's two-factor from Users or with
  `sibuna console reset-factor <id> --revision <n>`. The reset checks the account revision,
  ends its sessions and cannot target the administrator's own account.
- Changes are audited as totp.disable, totp.reset and totp.recovery.

Upgrade:
- The console schema moves to version 46 on first start. Earlier binaries refuse to start
  against it, so upgrade every node of a cluster and do not downgrade afterwards.
- Give every console node the same --console-key-file; a node with a different key cannot
  read factors enrolled elsewhere.

Qualification:
- Storage, HTTP route and console rendering tests cover replay, stale revisions, forged
  recovery values, unreadable factors, session revocation and audit records.
- The console end-to-end suite runs the release executable through code replacement, turning
  two-factor off, re-enrollment, sign-in after a console key change, and an administrator
  reset through the CLI, within the production sign-in limits.
- The full native suite, console browser tests and documentation build pass on a clean
  checkout: 110 of 110 build steps and 1,181 of 1,181 tests. The console end-to-end suite
  also passes on a cluster build, including three-node failover and quorum loss.
- A console database created and used by the published v0.3.1 binary migrates on first start;
  the same account then reads its two-factor status and enrolls. On v0.3.1 that status read
  answered 503.
- The release workflow builds and checks every packaged executable before publication.
- Benchmarks and the FTW corpus results in the v0.3.0 notes still apply, because the request
  path is unchanged.

Downloads:
- Linux x86-64 and ARM64: statically linked musl builds; Linux 5.10 or later.
- macOS Apple Silicon and Intel: macOS 15 or later; unsigned command-line builds.
- Windows x86-64: native sibuna.exe; Windows 10 / Server 2019 or later.

Archives include the executable, README, full license texts, dependency notices and an exact
build manifest. SHA256SUMS covers every archive. Engine sources are LGPL-3.0; console
sources, including the Wasm interface, are AGPL-3.0. The combined executable is AGPL-covered.
CRS rules are Apache-2.0 and are downloaded and verified at runtime, not bundled.
Corresponding source and build scripts are in this release's tag and linked from the console.
Companies seeking alternative licensing can contact the authors, Vikrant Rathore and
Ronak Rathore. Third-party libraries remain subject to their respective licenses.

The shipped builds include storage and console support; the console starts only with --console.
Multi-node deployments require a separate -Dcluster=true build with OpenSSL 3. No GeoIP address
database is bundled; use the documented CLI import/update commands for your chosen dataset.

The v0.3.0 release notes describe that release's behaviour changes and limits, which still
apply: https://github.com/insanai/sibuna/releases/tag/v0.3.0

Documentation: https://insanai.github.io/sibuna/
Deployment guide: https://insanai.github.io/sibuna/book/operations.html
Source: https://github.com/insanai/sibuna/tree/v0.3.2
